shortSummary: Erect annual medicinal herb renowned as 'King of Bitters' for fiercely bitter andrographolide diterpenoids supporting hepatoprotective and upper-respiratory defense.
leadOverview: Andrographis paniculata—celebrated across Bengal homesteads and Ayurvedic clinics as Kalomegh ('Dark Cloud')—is a slender, square-stemmed herbaceous herb of the acanthus family Acanthaceae. Known globally as the 'King of Bitters' (and regionally traded alongside Chirata), its lance-shaped dark leaves pack potent andrographolide lactones widely studied for immune resilience and liver protection.

sections.title: Morphological Description
sections.subtitle: Jointed square green stems, lanceolate leaves, spotted white bilabiate blooms, and linear capsules
sections.summary: Anatomy of four-angled herbaceous shoots, opposite simple leaves, two-lipped white flowers, and spring-loaded pods.
paragraphs: Andrographis paniculata grows as an upright, neatly branched herbaceous annual reaching 30 to 110 centimetres tall on smooth dark-green quadrangular stems noticeably swollen at every leaf-bearing node. Its opposite, short-stalked leaves are lance-shaped with tapered tips (5–10 cm long), deep glossy green above and paler beneath, tasting intensely bitter from just a pinpoint nibble.

From late Borsha through Hemonto, loose airy panicles rise from upper leaf axils bearing small dainty white two-lipped flowers (1–1.5 cm) prettily flecked with magenta-purple stripes inside the lower lip. Following pollination, slender cylindrical capsules (1.5–2 cm) ripen pale tan and snap open explosively to flick out 8 to 12 yellowish-brown warty seeds.

subblocks.heading: Swollen Quadrangular Nodes
subblocks.text: Four-angled emerald stems slightly winged along corners with characteristic Acanthaceae nodal joints.

subblocks.heading: Lanceolate Bitter Foliage
subblocks.text: Opposite smooth glabrous blades storing up to 2–3% dry weight of andrographolide lactones.

subblocks.heading: Purple-Spotted Bilabiate Flowers
subblocks.text: Tubular white corollas divided into an upper hood and spotted three-lobed lower landing lip.

subblocks.heading: Ballochorous Seed Capsules
subblocks.text: Linear two-valved pods lined with curved hook-like retinacula that catapult dry seeds cleanly away.

sections.title: Taxonomy & Botanical Classification
sections.subtitle: Lamiales Acanthaceae lineage and distinction from Himalayan Chirata
sections.summary: Taxonomic placement in Acanthaceae and widespread trade as 'Deshi Chirata' across Bengal.
paragraphs: Classified in order Lamiales and family Acanthaceae—sharing swollen stem joints and two-lipped flowers with Vasaka/Basok (Justicia adhatoda) and Mangrove Acanthus—Andrographis paniculata was first described by Nicolaas Laurens Burman before Christian Gottfried Nees von Esenbeck assigned its modern genus in 1832.

In village herb markets across Bangladesh, Kalomegh is commonly sold as 'Deshi Chirata' or 'Chirota' as a lowland substitute for rare endangered Himalayan Swertia chirayita (Gentianaceae), though the two plants belong to entirely separate families.

sections.title: Natural Habitat & Global Distribution
sections.subtitle: Shaded village groves, forest clearings, and Natore medicinal herb farms
sections.summary: Native across India, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka with vigorous commercial farming in northern Bengal.
paragraphs: Native to shaded woodland edges, bamboo thickets, and fallow uplands across India, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka, Kalmegh naturally germinates with early pre-monsoon rains and completes its reproductive cycle across autumn.

Today it is cultivated commercially across Natore's Kholabaria, Bogura, Tangail, and Madhupur agro-herb corridors as well as Thailand ('Fah Talai Jone') and Scandinavia (standardized into Kan Jang immune extracts).

sections.title: Ecological Role & Pollinator Interactions
sections.subtitle: Herbivore deterrence via diterpene bitterness and explosive seed scatter
sections.summary: Chemical bitterness deterring grazing livestock and elastic capsule dispersal along shaded banks.
paragraphs: Because intensely bitter andrographolides deter goats, cattle, and chewing caterpillars almost completely, Kalmegh survives unprotected along rural footpaths where tender grasses are cropped short.
Tiny sweat bees and hoverflies visit magenta-guided white blossoms in autumn before dry winter air triggers snapping seed pods to broadcast fresh seeds up to 2 metres around parent clumps.

sections.title: Economic, Culinary & Cultural Importance
sections.subtitle: Morning Chirata water, Kalmegh Bori pills, and global botanical immune trade
sections.summary: Everyday rural Bengali bitter digestive routine alongside growing international herbal demand.
paragraphs: Across rural and urban Bengal alike, steeping dried Kalomegh/Chirota twigs overnight in half a glass of cool water to sip first thing on an empty morning stomach remains a deeply rooted seasonal wellness habit believed to balance sluggish appetite and post-monsoon biliousness.

Traditional apothecaries roll pounded fresh Kalomegh juice with crushed black pepper or turmeric into tiny sun-dried 'Kalmegh Bori' pellets—masking the bracing bitterness for easier administration—while Thailand and Europe manufacture standardized capsules at industrial scale.

sections.title: Traditional & Scientific Medicinal Properties
sections.subtitle: Andrographolide NF-kB modulation, upper-respiratory trials, and hepatic support
sections.summary: Randomized trials on acute viral upper-respiratory recovery alongside strict pregnancy & drug cautions.
paragraphs: Known in Ayurveda as 'Bhunimba' ('Earth Neem') and 'Kalamegha', aerial shoots owe primary bioactivity to labdane diterpenoid lactones—especially andrographolide, neoandrographolide, and 14-deoxyandrographolide—that show hepatoprotective and NF-kappaB inflammatory-pathway modulation in preclinical studies.

Multiple systematic reviews and randomized human trials report modest, statistically significant reductions in symptom severity and duration of uncomplicated acute upper respiratory tract colds when standardized Andrographis extract is started early.
sections.safetyNote: Avoid Kalmegh strictly during pregnancy (may exert uterine/anti-implantation effects) and breastfeeding. Because andrographolide can stimulate immunity, lower blood pressure/glucose, and inhibit CYP450 enzymes, consult a physician if managing autoimmune disease or taking anticoagulants, antihypertensives, or immunosuppressants.

sections.title: Comprehensive Cultivation & Care Guide
sections.subtitle: Intercropping under orchard shade, monsoon sowing, and pre-bloom harvest timing
sections.summary: Growing lush bitter shoots cleanly in partial-shade garden beds or 10-inch balcony pots.
paragraphs: Sow tiny seeds thinly over damp composted nursery beds (pH 5.8–7.5) at monsoon onset without burying deeply—light aids germination within 7 to 10 days. Transplant seedlings at 20-by-20-centimetre spacing into backyard flower beds, balcony containers, or shaded mango/banana orchard intercrops.

Plants need zero chemical pesticides thanks to natural bitter deterrence. Harvest entire aerial shoots 10 centimetres above ground right as the first flower buds appear in late Shorot (90–110 days after planting)—when andrographolide concentration peaks—then dry promptly in clean shade.

sections.title: Annual Phenology & Six-Season Rhythms
sections.subtitle: Flowering, fruiting, vegetative flush, and Shororitu synchrony
sections.summary: Seasonal cadence across Bengal's six-season cycle (Monsoon (বর্ষা), Autumn (শরৎ), Late Autumn (হেমন্ত)).
paragraphs: Kalmegh (King of Bitters) (Andrographis paniculata) aligns its vegetative flushes, anthesis, and fruit maturation tightly with Bengal's Shororitu photoperiod and monsoon moisture transitions, showing peak biological activity during Monsoon (বর্ষা), Autumn (শরৎ), Late Autumn (হেমন্ত).

Monsoon (বর্ষা): Monsoon seedlings establish upright square green stems rich in bitter andrographolide foliage. Autumn (শরৎ): Pre-bloom leaf potency peaks just as delicate magenta-flecked white flowers begin opening. Late Autumn (হেমন্ত): Snapping two-valved linear capsules disperse seeds across shaded Natore herb plots and gardens.

sections.title: Seed Germination Biology & Propagation
sections.subtitle: Dormancy regulation, nursery media, and clonal propagation
sections.summary: Reproductive biology and reliable seed or vegetative propagation techniques for Kalmegh (King of Bitters).
paragraphs: Kalmegh (King of Bitters) (Andrographis paniculata) exhibits dual reproductive versatility through wind-, pollinator-, or gravity-dispersed seed cohorts alongside rapid vegetative renewal via herbaceous stem cuttings, rhizome splits, or nodal rooting. Mature seed capsules collected just prior to dehiscence retain strong vigor in dry shaded storage for moderate periods.
Rooting auxin pre-treatment on semi-ripe nodal cuttings during warm humid months accelerates adventitious root initiation within 10 to 21 days in porous coco-peat and vermicompost propagation trays.

subblocks.heading: Seed Germination
subblocks.text: Surface-sown or lightly covered in sterile porous mix; germinates in 7–21 days under ambient humidity.

subblocks.heading: Vegetative Method
subblocks.text: Two-node terminal cuttings or clump division rooted in misted, filtered-light benches.

sections.title: Pathology Defense, Vectors & Organic IPM
sections.subtitle: Phytoalexin resilience, fungal prophylaxis, and predator guilds
sections.summary: Biochemical defense mechanisms and low-impact organic IPM guidelines for Andrographis paniculata.
paragraphs: In humid South Asian and tropical growing belts, Kalmegh (King of Bitters) (Andrographis paniculata) relies on secondary terpenoid resins, foliar trichomes, and phytoalexin phenolics as front-line biochemical deterrence against herbivores and opportunistic pathogens. Prolonged monsoon waterlogging or stagnant canopy humidity can nonetheless encourage anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.), powdery mildew, leaf-spot fungi, or root-zone Pythium.

Organic Integrated Pest Management (IPM) prioritizes preventive airflow pruning, Trichoderma-enriched compost amendments around feeder roots, and targeted cold-pressed Azadirachta indica (neem) oil sprays at dusk to suppress sap-sucking aphids, scale insects, and mealybugs without harming native pollinators.

subblocks.heading: Fungal Management
subblocks.text: Prevent overhead foliar wetness at dusk; maintain canopy aeration and copper/Trichoderma prophylaxis.

subblocks.heading: Organic Pest Control
subblocks.text: Neem kernel emulsion (3–5 ml/L) plus conservation of hoverfly and ladybird predator guilds.

sections.title: Conservation Standing & Climate Resilience
sections.subtitle: Population security, agroforestry corridors, and stress tolerance
sections.summary: Biogeographic conservation standing and climate adaptation traits of Kalmegh (King of Bitters).
paragraphs: Across its native and naturalized distribution (South Asia (India, Bangladesh & Sri Lanka)), Kalmegh (King of Bitters) (Andrographis paniculata) demonstrates strong ecological plasticity across alluvial floodplains, homestead agroforestry plots, and urban biodiversity corridors. While cultivated stands remain broadly secure, landrace genetic erosion, coastal salinity shifts, and wetland drainage threaten wild ecotypes and heritage regional varieties.

Long-term resilience depends on decentralized in-situ homestead stewardship, wetland buffer conservation, and botanical garden germplasm collections preserving drought-, flood-, and salinity-tolerant alleles amid shifting monsoon regimes.

subblocks.heading: Ecological Resilience
subblocks.text: Adapted to South Asia (India, Bangladesh & Sri Lanka) thermal oscillations and seasonal hydrological extremes.

subblocks.heading: Stewardship Strategy
subblocks.text: Preserve traditional landraces, pollinator corridors, and living herbarium voucher plots.

sections.title: Horticultural Spacing, Pruning & Telemetry
sections.subtitle: Plot geometry, canopy shaping, and calibrated soil-climate meters
sections.summary: Calibrated horticultural parameters: pH 5.8 – 7.5, Light Shade to Bright Sun, and structural spacing guidance.
paragraphs: Optimal managed cultivation of Kalmegh (King of Bitters) (Andrographis paniculata) calibrates root-zone chemistry around pH 5.8 – 7.5 inside moist sandy-clay garden loam. Providing adequate crown spacing prevents humidity buildup and lets lower shoots capture uniform irradiance across light shade to bright sun.

Light corrective pruning immediately after main flowering or harvest periods redirects assimilates into healthy vegetative framework, while moisture scheduling (moderate monsoon / drained) stabilizes root turgor without inducing hypoxia.

sections.title: Evolutionary Genetics & Adaptive Phylogeny
sections.subtitle: Lamiales clade divergence and Acanthaceae genomic traits
sections.summary: Phylogenetic placement of genus Andrographis within order Lamiales (Eudicot (Lamiids)).
paragraphs: Modern molecular phylogenetics (APG IV) places Andrographis paniculata inside family Acanthaceae (অ্যাকান্থাসি (কালমেঘ-বাসক গোত্র)), order Lamiales, clade Eudicot (Lamiids). Medicinal herbs and coastal shrubs recognized by swollen stem nodes above opposite leaves, two-lipped flowers, and explosively dehiscent seed capsules.

Within genus Andrographis, specialized morphological adaptations—such as distinctively swollen jointed nodes along quadrangular herbaceous stems—reflect co-evolutionary specialization with regional pollinator guilds and abiotic habitat filters.

sections.title: Field Identification Key & Diagnostic Checks
sections.subtitle: Macro-morphological verification against look-alike taxa
sections.summary: Rapid field-sheet checklist for confirming Andrographis paniculata (Kalomegh / Chirata (কালমেঘ)).
paragraphs: Field verification of Kalmegh (King of Bitters) (Andrographis paniculata) rests on recognizing key Acanthaceae family markers: Distinctively swollen jointed nodes along quadrangular herbaceous stems; Bilabiate spotted corollas often framed by conspicuous floral bracts; Linear two-valved capsules hurling seeds via curved hook-like retinacula. Inspecting fresh leaf arrangement, stem surface texture, and reproductive architecture together eliminates confusion with sympatric congeners.

Swollen Quadrangular Nodes: Four-angled emerald stems slightly winged along corners with characteristic Acanthaceae nodal joints. Lanceolate Bitter Foliage: Opposite smooth glabrous blades storing up to 2–3% dry weight of andrographolide lactones. Purple-Spotted Bilabiate Flowers: Tubular white corollas divided into an upper hood and spotted three-lobed lower landing lip. Ballochorous Seed Capsules: Linear two-valved pods lined with curved hook-like retinacula that catapult dry seeds cleanly away.
